title: Networks, complexes, reactions; the complex set
assessment: Complexes are natural stoichiometric vectors; reactions retain explicit source and target, including indexed parallel channels and self-loops. The two membership lemmas are the advertised elementary facts.

title: Linkage classes are the connected components of the reaction graph
assessment: Linkage classes are the quotient by undirected reachability and their number equals connected-component cardinality. No graph connectivity is silently assumed.

title: Weakly reversible iff every strong linkage class is terminal
assessment: Weak reversibility is target-to-source reachability for every reaction; the terminal-strong-class equivalence has the expected quantifiers.

title: Conservation laws: dimension of the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace
assessment: Conservation laws are the real orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric span; the dimension formula uses finite species and natural subtraction with rank bounded by species count.

title: Deficiency `δ = n − ℓ − s ≥ 0`; `δ = dim(ker Y ∩ im ∂)`
assessment: The integer deficiency is n-l-s; nonnegativity and its identification with the kernel/image intersection dimension are separate substantive results.

title: `∑ δᵢ ≤ δ`, with equality characterized
assessment: The inequality is established. The cited equality characterization merely says equality iff the reverse numerical inequality, using the already proved inequality. It does not characterize independent linkage stoichiometric subspaces. See R11.

title: Siphons; the zero set of an ω-limit point is a siphon
assessment: The omega-limit zero-set result requires a compact containing set, nonnegative omega-limit points, and genuine mass-action dynamics on those points. These are explicit dynamical hypotheses, not purely graph assumptions.

title: Mass action; the closed orthant is forward invariant
assessment: The cited Nagumo lemma is for a supplied differentiable trajectory and a linear lower bound near negative coordinates. Mass-action lower-bound and positivity bridges supply that analytic input; the lemma alone is not an existence theorem.

title: General kinetic systems; deficiency-zero conclusions without mass action
reference: Feinberg 1972 (Complex balancing in general kinetic systems); Feinberg 2019, ch. on general kinetics
assessment: At deficiency zero stationary flux is graph balanced for arbitrary kinetics. Non-weak-reversibility excludes stationary or closed trajectories with strictly positive reaction rates; positivity and continuity assumptions are retained.

title: Generalized mass action / power-law systems
assessment: Arbitrary real kinetic orders are represented. Generalized existence uses zero kinetic deficiency plus explicit sign-closure/equal-dimension conditions; ordinary deficiency zero alone is not enough. The sign criterion addresses uniqueness separately.

title: Michaelis–Menten and Hill kinetics
assessment: Hill and Michaelis-Menten rate laws and their admissibility are concrete. The cited qssa_error_bound is a conditional defect/Gronwall estimate, not by itself a derivation of the Michaelis-Menten reduction; concrete enzyme estimates are under D19.

title: `ẋ = Y A_κ Ψ(x)`; the matrix-tree theorem for the kinetic Laplacian
assessment: The actual mass-action field factors through the complex Laplacian. The directed tree/cofactor identity is proved by a determinant argument; F17 explains the linkage restriction.

title: Open systems (CFSTR): zero complex and inflow/outflow pseudo-reactions
assessment: fullyOpen adds positive inflow and outflow for every species. The zero/one-deficiency existence and uniqueness statements keep their weak-reversibility/deficiency hypotheses. Partially open conservation identities do not imply these stronger equilibrium conclusions.

title: Elementary flux modes are the extreme rays of the flux cone
assessment: For the nonnegative stationary-flux cone, nonzero support-minimal fluxes are exactly extreme-ray generators and generate the cone. Reversible channels are represented as separate nonnegative coordinates, not unrestricted signed reaction rates.

title: Circulations on the reaction graph decompose into cycles
assessment: Nonnegative graph-balanced reaction fluxes decompose as finite nonnegative sums of directed cycle flows. This is graph circulation, distinct from merely stoichiometrically stationary flux.

title: Conservation laws are constants of motion
assessment: A real left-kernel weight has constant pairing along a supplied mass-action solution. The interval and derivative hypotheses are explicit.

title: The directed matrix-tree theorem in cofactor form
assessment: The always-positive cofactor is taken inside the root's linkage block. A full-matrix cofactor can vanish in a disconnected network; separate theorems state this distinction correctly.

title: Subnetwork and embedded-network theory
assessment: Reaction restriction and species projection are genuine network constructions with containment/projection identities. Their existence does not assert preservation of every dynamical property.

title: Detailed balance and the Wegscheider conditions
assessment: A reversible pairing and log equilibrium constants are explicit. SatisfiesWegscheider is orthogonality to the stationary-flux kernel; S22 supplies the existence converse. Aggregate and reactionwise detailed balance are distinguished.

title: Positive complex-balanced equilibria form a log-linear (toric) set
assessment: Given a positive complex-balanced reference, positive complex-balanced states are its multiplicative exponential translate of the stoichiometric orthogonal complement.

title: Exactly one complex-balanced equilibrium in each positive class
assessment: The field-map citation only proves at most one. Existence for every positive class is provided elsewhere by exists_isComplexBalanced_in_positiveClass/Birch, so the combined exactly-one claim is supported.

title: A positive complex-balanced equilibrium forces weak reversibility
assessment: Positive complex balance with strictly positive rate constants implies graph weak reversibility; no equilibrium-existence assumption is hidden beyond the supplied reference.

title: Complex balanced for every κ iff weakly reversible and `δ = 0`
assessment: For every positive rate vector, existence of some positive complex-balanced point is equivalent to weak reversibility and deficiency zero. The rate quantifier is universal, not existential.

title: For `δ = 0`, every positive steady state is complex balanced
assessment: The cited positiveSteadyState_iff_complexBalanced assumes existence of a positive complex-balanced reference and is stronger than the deficiency-zero special case once existence is supplied by S5. Keep that reference premise when quoting it.

title: Complex balance iff the tree-constant binomials vanish
assessment: Tree-constant binomials characterize positive complex balance under weak reversibility. The ordinary theorem keeps positivity; generalized power-law monomials use their own domain convention.

title: The steady-state ideal of a WR `δ = 0` network agrees on the positive torus with the binomial ideal
assessment: The two actual multivariate-polynomial ideals have the same positive real vanishing set for weakly reversible deficiency-zero networks. This is positive-torus equivalence, not equality of ideals or of their complex varieties.

title: Birch's theorem
assessment: For every positive reference and positive affine-class representative there exists exactly one positive point in the affine class with orthogonal log-ratio. This is the required real Birch intersection theorem.

title: Deficiency zero theorem
assessment: The named conclusion expands to unique positive complex balance in every positive compatibility class, for every rate vector, from weak reversibility and deficiency zero. Dynamics are separate theorems.

title: Deficiency one theorem (existence and uniqueness)
assessment: DeficiencyOneHypotheses records each linkage deficiency at most one, additivity of deficiencies, and one terminal strong class per linkage class. Uniqueness uses that package; weak-reversible existence is separate and also follows from S12.

title: Weakly reversible mass action has a positive steady state in every class
assessment: Every weakly reversible network, every positive rate vector, and every positive compatibility class have a positive steady state. There is no deficiency restriction or supplied steady-state witness.

title: Absolute concentration robustness for deficiency one
assessment: The fixed-rate Shinar-Feinberg theorem keeps deficiency one, two nonterminal complexes differing only in the robust species, and existence of a positive steady state at that rate. The all-rate version explicitly requires existence at every rate.

title: Network translation and generalized complex balance
assessment: Translation gives correct conditional field/balance bridges, but SteadyStateFaithfulOn assumes the difficult original-steady-state-to-translated-balance implication. The cited iff does not derive that implication from a general translation criterion. See R12.

title: Linear conjugacy of mass-action systems
assessment: Positive diagonal conjugacy is characterized by source-wise weighted reaction sums and yields Jacobian similarity. A conjugate-network search algorithm is not supplied.

title: Generalized mass action: complex balance and a Birch-type theorem
assessment: Universal uniqueness is characterized by a sign-vector intersection condition. Generalized existence retains kinetic-deficiency and sign-closure hypotheses; it is not an unconditional Birch theorem for arbitrary kinetic orders.

title: Linear elimination; MESSI systems; toric steady states; rational parametrizations; steady-state invariants
reference: Feliu–Wiuf 2012; Pérez Millán–Dickenstein 2018; Pérez Millán et al. 2012; Thomson–Gunawardena 2009
assessment: The binomial/logarithmic parametrization and disjoint-support criterion are substantive. MESSI is a different, singleton-source class, and exponential parametrization is not a constructed rational parametrization. Published MESSI coverage is not established. See R1.

title: Bounds on the number of positive steady states
assessment: Bounds/classifications are for specified one-species, rank-one, two-reaction, and decorated-cell systems with their nonzero-polynomial, sign, or nondegeneracy hypotheses. These do not give a general count bound for arbitrary networks.

title: The number of positive steady states of a fully open network is odd
assessment: The general parity theorem assumes finite zeros, nondegeneracy, no boundary zeros, and an odd/prescribed class degree. Full openness alone does not imply oddness: the audit exhibits exactly two positive steady states. See R2.

title: The nilpotent-Jacobian criterion for complex-balanced equilibria
assessment: At a positive complex-balanced equilibrium, nilpotence plus entropy-metric dissipation forces the actual Jacobian to vanish and every positive-flux reaction vector to vanish. This is valid; identifying arbitrary adjacency spectra with the Jacobian is not used.

title: The King–Altman formula: the steady state of a unimolecular network is a ratio of spanning trees
assessment: Tree ratios produce a normalized steady state for singleton-to-singleton transfer networks. Positivity requires weak reversibility and occurring species; uniqueness up to one scalar additionally requires a single linkage class and no unused species.

title: The Wegscheider converse
assessment: For an explicit reversible pairing, Wegscheider conditions are equivalent to a log potential and to a positive reactionwise detailed-balanced state.

title: Perron–Frobenius theory for primitive nonnegative matrices
assessment: The cited primitive-matrix statements prove nonnilpotence/nonzero eigenvalues and conditional Collatz-Wielandt bounds, not the full Perron root, simplicity, and spectral-dominance theorem. The prose acknowledges this but the proved label/title overreach. See R11.

title: The equilibrium depends smoothly on the rate constants
assessment: A nondegenerate equilibrium has a local C1 rate-parameter branch, and orientation persists locally. This is not a global selection or a theorem for degenerate equilibria; the named branch theorem states C1 rather than arbitrary smoothness.

title: An injective network has at most one steady state per class
assessment: Injectivity on a positive stoichiometric class implies at most one positive steady state in that class. No existence or stability conclusion is inferred.

title: P-matrix Jacobians and Gale–Nikaido univalence
assessment: The field-map entry points to a local-homeomorphism lemma, but the full unconditional finite-dimensional box injectivity theorem exists as CRNT.injOn_of_pmatrix_fderiv in GaleNikaidoUniv. The mathematics is supported; the citation should point there.

title: The species–reaction graph theorem
assessment: The true-chemistry SR criterion proves injectivity/strong concordance under reactant-product separation, the specified flow convention, and normality where required. These restrictions are part of the published graph setting, not arbitrary-graph conclusions.

title: DSR graph criteria
assessment: DSR oriented-cycle and s-cycle conditions yield concordance/injectivity for the fully open extension under separation and singleton-flow restrictions. The determinant expansion alone would not establish this; the later bridge does.

title: Concordance iff injectivity for every weakly monotonic kinetics
assessment: Concordance is equivalent to interior class injectivity for every weakly monotonic admissible kinetics. The cited paper also includes a nonnegative boundary point paired with a positive point; that stronger boundary-inclusive injectivity is not the predicate here. See R16.

title: Strong concordance for fully open and weakly reversible networks
assessment: Strong concordance transfers from the fully open extension to a weakly reversible, reactant-product-separated network. It is not a theorem that weak reversibility alone implies strong concordance.

title: Deficiency One Algorithm
assessment: Capacity is equivalent to a semantic real log-ratio/positive-flux certificate. DOAAffirmsCapacity and arbitrary shelf-run correctness are separate and incomplete. No finite published Deficiency One Algorithm is verified. See R15.

title: Advanced Deficiency Algorithm
assessment: ADAFeasible supplies shelf-wise real flux/exponential balances, and capacity supplies a one-shelf witness. This is not an end-to-end finite Ellison algorithm or an arbitrary multi-shelf construction. See R15.

title: Brouwer degree and steady-state existence
assessment: Finite signed counts yield existence and conditional degree-counting arguments. Rate homotopies require all intermediate zeros to remain regular; general boundary-avoiding Brouwer degree and the dissipative total-degree calculation are missing. See R8.

title: Capacity tests: two positive zeros, sign-indefinite reduced Jacobian
assessment: The cited sign-indefinite test already assumes two positive zeros. The stronger one-exceptional-sign argument elsewhere assumes the total class degree; it does not derive that degree from dissipativity. See R8.

title: Inheritance of multistationarity; atoms of multistationarity
assessment: Adding small-rate reactions preserves nondegenerate positive equilibria for full-rank networks or for dependent reaction additions relative to the class. Embedded rank-one lifts and atom examples are present, not an unrestricted inheritance theorem.

title: Interconnection of networks injective on their classes
assessment: The only cited theorem assumes injectivity of the combined vector field. It does not infer this from injectivity of the components. Components x'=x and x'=-x are individually injective but cancel when interconnected. See R12.

title: Parameter regions for multistationarity
assessment: The sharp derivative-sign criterion is proved for compact rank-one classes without boundary equilibria; higher-rank regions and general algorithmic parameter partitions need the missing degree machinery.

title: Bounded forward solutions from positive states stay positive
assessment: A supplied global forward solution, initially positive and bounded above, remains positive. The result is a positivity statement, not a premise-free global existence theorem for arbitrary networks.

title: The relative entropy decreases along solutions
assessment: Relative entropy to a positive complex-balanced reference decreases along positive genuine mass-action solutions. The derivative is of the actual mass-action field, not a separate surrogate.

title: LaSalle's invariance principle
assessment: For a continuous semiflow with a compact absorbing tail and a continuous nonincreasing Lyapunov function, the omega-limit set is nonempty, invariant, and has constant Lyapunov value. Later lemmas identify the zero-dissipation invariant set.

title: Local asymptotic stability of the complex-balanced equilibrium in its class
assessment: Local entropy-sublevel confinement, actual forward solutions, uniqueness in class, and local exponential entropy decay provide the claimed class-relative local asymptotic stability. It is not stability in directions transverse to conserved quantities.

title: Global Attractor Theorem for complex-balanced systems
assessment: The trajectory theorem has ordinary mass-action derivatives and genuine Tendsto. The audit constructs a global forward solution and convergence with only positive complex balance and class compatibility. Ambient-flow wrappers can be vacuous, but this result is not. See the detailed GAC audit.

title: GAC for a single linkage class
assessment: The original cited singleLinkageClass_gac carries persistence, but singleLinkageClass_gac_unconditional discharges it via strong endotacticity. D5 also supplies the general conclusion.

title: No critical siphon ⇒ persistence
assessment: No critical siphon gives boundary-omega exclusion under the supplied bounded-flow hypotheses. Strong compact-confinement persistence additionally needs upper boundedness, here supplied in the complex-balanced/deficiency-zero route.

title: Endotactic networks; weakly reversible ⇒ endotactic
assessment: EndotacticStd is the published essential-source condition; Endotactic is weaker. Both are defined and their difference is explicitly refuted by an example. Weak reversibility implies the standard predicate, so the intended conclusion is available.

title: Strongly endotactic networks are permanent
assessment: StronglyEndotacticStd.permanent_varK states class-uniform compact interior tail absorption for every genuine forward solution with rates in a fixed positive band. This retains the tempered-rate quantifiers of the deterministic theorem.

title: Weakly reversible processes near facets
assessment: The facet theorem retains the rank-at-most-one projected stoichiometric condition and gives coordinatewise inward field near the face. A separate bounded-WR floor result removes the facet restriction for bounded orbit closure.

title: No drainable siphon ⇒ persistence; autocatalysis
assessment: Drainability/self-replication use executable finite reaction pathways. Absence of drainable siphons excludes finite boundary orbit-closure points, including the unbounded-orbit formulation; boundedness is needed to turn that into compact confinement.

title: Persistence conjecture
reference: Feinberg 1987; Craciun–Nazarov–Pantea 2013; Pantea 2012; Craciun, arXiv:1501.02860 v3 (§8 remark)
assessment: The genuine-trajectory coordinate floor proves persistence for bounded weakly reversible trajectories in all dimensions. Conservative networks supply boundedness. Unbounded WR trajectories and the stronger global boundedness/confinement conjecture are not settled by this theorem.

title: Conservative networks have compact compatibility classes
assessment: A strictly positive conservation weight bounds every nonnegative class coordinate; closedness then gives compactness. The reference state is required nonnegative.

title: Monotone systems and contraction for reaction networks
assessment: The contraction, Kamke, and strong-order propagation fragments are useful. The claimed Hirsch generic convergence uses a coercively increasing vector field, a strict LaSalle certificate, and uniqueness of equilibria, not the classical almost-everywhere strong-flow result. See R3.

title: Routh–Hurwitz criteria (degree ≤ 4)
assessment: Quadratic through quartic Hurwitz tests have correct coefficient and root-conjugacy conditions; polynomial-level bridges remove the supplied-root representation. Crossing gates are distinct from nonlinear Hopf existence.

title: Hopf bifurcation
assessment: Spectral crossing gates, cubic normal-form algebra, coefficient calibration, and periodic orbits of the truncation are proved. The mass-action-named verdict does not assert a solution of the original network. See R4.

title: Weakly reversible deficiency zero networks have no positive periodic orbits
assessment: PositivePeriodicOrbit requires genuine derivatives, positivity, a positive period, and nonconstancy. Complex-balanced Lyapunov descent rules it out; weakly reversible deficiency zero provides complex balance for every rate.

title: Existence of oscillations; chaos
assessment: The Lotka positive periodic-orbit witness and time averages are genuine. General Poincare-Bendixson/no-chaos statements still consume an unconstructed planar kernel; the chaos predicate is a bespoke minimal-set classification. See R7.

title: Quasi-steady-state reduction; Tikhonov–Fenichel
assessment: Concrete enzyme tracking and slow-fast error estimates are valid conditional results. fenichel_persistence only gives discrete-time invariance from supplied graph transforms; full normally hyperbolic manifold persistence is not proved. AllTimeRegraph even forces the fixed operator to be identity. See R5.

title: Intermediates and their elimination
assessment: Drained noninteracting intermediates have a uniquely solvable linear subsystem, positive monomial elimination coefficients, and a Schur-complement reduced field. Drainage is derived from network reachability. This is steady-state elimination, not automatically dynamical QSSA.

title: The linearization at a complex-balanced equilibrium
assessment: A positive complex-balanced equilibrium admits a strict quadratic Lyapunov function on the stoichiometric subspace and is Hurwitz there. Conservation-induced ambient zero eigenvalues are correctly excluded from this restriction.

title: Rate-sensitive stability: exponentially converging rate constants
assessment: Exponentially convergent rates plus a limiting contraction bound, boundedness, and confinement give quantitative exponential convergence. This is a contraction theorem, not unrestricted nonautonomous CRNT stability.

title: Global asymptotic stability under persistence
assessment: Given compact positive confinement of genuine forward trajectories, the cutoff construction produces a global genuine orbit and its singleton omega-limit; the eventual convergence bridge uses compactness. Persistence is an explicit premise.

title: The chemical master equation generator
assessment: The falling-factorial stochastic mass-action generator and the minimal transition recursion are concrete. Forward-CME derivatives keep their required summability assumptions; zero-order and monomolecular identities use the expected rates.

title: Product-form Poisson stationary distributions iff complex balance
assessment: Positive product-Poisson master stationarity is equivalent to complex balance. Separate summability, normalization, and semigroup-invariance theorems make this more than a merely algebraic residual identity.

title: Stochastic detailed balance from the Wegscheider conditions
assessment: An explicit reversible pairing and Wegscheider conditions produce a positive parameter satisfying reactionwise microscopic detailed balance of the falling-factorial rates and Poisson weights.

title: Convergence to stationarity on a finite closed strongly connected region
assessment: The old regionMatrix convergence result requires entrywise positivity, stronger than strong connectivity. The newer MinimalSemigroupErgodic result establishes continuous-time convergence on finite closed irreducible regions. Do not quote the old discrete-time statement without its extra hypothesis.

title: Absorbing states
assessment: IsAbsorbingCount means no reaction is enabled, which is a deadlock condition. For allowed self-loop reactions it is stricter than Markov-state absorption (no state-changing jumps). The forward implication remains valid. See R13.

title: Foster–Lyapunov criteria
assessment: Embedded-chain survival/hitting bounds and minimal-semigroup Foster results are proved from explicit nonnegative Lyapunov/drift data. Path-space hitting random variables are not constructed, so the interpretation should remain at the proved kernel/survival level.

title: Positive recurrence and non-explosivity on infinite state spaces
assessment: The minimal semigroup, conservative non-explosion, drift criteria, restricted stochastic endotactic classes, and examples are substantive. Strong endotacticity alone does not imply stochastic recurrence/non-explosion; the cited paper refutes that universal claim. See R6.

title: Kurtz's law of large numbers
assessment: Generator convergence, conditional deterministic fluid bounds, Poisson-clock concentration, and fixed-time monomolecular LLN are present. A time-indexed CRN path process with filtration and a process-level Skorokhod LLN remain absent.

title: Central limit theorem; diffusion (chemical Langevin) approximation
assessment: Nonlinear fixed-time multivariate Gaussian limits are genuine weak-convergence theorems, including a defect-completed law for possibly explosive chains near an equilibrium. They do not establish a trajectory-space functional CLT or an SDE/chemical-Langevin path approximation.

title: Extinction in networks with absolute concentration robustness
assessment: Conservative deficiency-one networks with a positive deterministic steady state and the specified nonterminal domination/kernel condition exhibit stochastic extinction of nonterminal complexes. Finite closed-class graph arguments are connected to absorption probabilities and transition limits.

title: Siphons correspond to prime supports
assessment: CoordinatePrimeContains is defined as a support test and IsSiphonPrimeSupport as that same siphon closure plus nonemptiness. No actual polynomial ideal, minimal prime, or primary-decomposition theorem appears in this file. See R9.

title: Elimination and Gröbner bases for steady-state ideals
assessment: Actual polynomial ideals, monomial saturation implications, elimination, Groebner bases, division, existence, and Buchberger-style criteria are represented mathematically. This does not promise an executable comprehensive Groebner solver.

title: Real root bounds and mixed volumes
assessment: Univariate Descartes bounds, circuit bounds, patchworking, determinant-defined zonotope mixed volumes, and separated-variable root bounds are present. General sparse BKK with multiplicities and arbitrary Newton polytopes is not proved; the volume-measure bridge is also incomplete. See R11.

title: Tropical model reduction
assessment: Valuation limits imply tropical balancing; lifting requires leading-system nondegeneracy. Local slow-fast estimates retain contraction/Hurwitz and domain hypotheses. The implicit-function critical graph should not be called an invariant perturbed slow manifold. See R5.

title: Identifiability of rate constants
assessment: Observational equality of full vector fields on the positive orthant is equivalent to equality of source-wise weighted reaction sums; all rates are identifiable exactly when outgoing vectors at each source are linearly independent. This is structural full-observation identifiability.

title: Entropy production is nonnegative for detailed-balanced systems; free energy beyond detailed balance
assessment: Entropy production, relative-entropy dissipation/minimization, and standard-potential Gibbs identities are proved under positivity and detailed/complex-balance or consistency conditions. These are ideal mass-action thermodynamics, not arbitrary nonideal thermodynamic models.

title: Reaction–diffusion systems; Turing instability
assessment: Two-species linear Turing inequalities and modal solutions are concrete; nonlinear existence is for a finite semidiscrete ODE. Global existence assumes global Lipschitz reaction terms. A nonlinear continuum reaction-diffusion PDE theorem is not supplied.

title: Non-isothermal and delay systems
assessment: Delayed production with instantaneous consumption has a genuine DDE, conservation/Lyapunov functionals, local existence/uniqueness, and global existence under positive weighted (sub)conservation. Nonisothermal identities are model-specific and do not yield a universal nonisothermal GAC.

title: Decision procedures (linkage, weak reversibility, deficiency, single-linkage GAC)
assessment: Finite structural decisions and exact rank/deficiency certificates are computationally checked. gac_of_singleLinkage_decide itself still takes persistence as a premise; unconditional single-linkage GAC exists elsewhere. Decision of structure is not decision of arbitrary dynamical properties.

title: Chemical computation
assessment: Stable computation uses the expected count reachability/output-stability quantifiers. Semilinear instead means finitely many natural-affine pieces over inequality regions; it excludes floor(n/2), although 2X to Y stably computes that function. There is no classical iff characterization. See R10.

title: Robust perfect adaptation; antithetic integral feedback
assessment: Steady-state and stationary-mean setpoints retain existence/integrability assumptions. Concrete closed-loop ergodicity and conditional general-plant drift transfers are proved; a general plant does not automatically supply the Foster certificate or guarantee adaptation. See R14.
